units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Right, let's brighten up. Rubens.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Peter Paul Rubens. The great painter of the 17th century.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Leader of the Antwerp school.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Wait. If the city was in decline, how did it have a star painter?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Good question. A city can lose its trade and still keep its talent.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Rubens led the Antwerp school of painters, and the city's churches and families kept him busy.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A bit of a comeback story.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Of a kind. In 1610 he bought a house in the city, a year after he married Isabella Brant.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: He rebuilt it in the style of an Italian palace, with a studio, a courtyard, and a Baroque garden.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: He built his own palazzo.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: With a workshop attached. He worked there with students and assistants, and he lived there until he died in 1640.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And you can go in.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The city bought the house in 1937, and it opened as a museum in 1946.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: One warning. At the time of writing, the main artist's residence section is closed for renovation.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: So check before you go.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Noted. Where are his paintings?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Four are in the Cathedral of Our Lady.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The Assumption of Mary over the high altar.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The Raising of the Cross and the Descent from the Cross on either side.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And a Resurrection of Christ in a side chapel.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Four in one church. That's a good start.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And his tomb is in a different church, Saint James's.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And there was also a printer?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Yes. Christophe Plantin. He moved from France around 1550 and built a printing house.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: His son-in-law, Jan Moretus, carried it on.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The building is now a museum with the two oldest surviving printing presses in the world.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Oldest in the world. Good fact for the pocket.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's a World Heritage Site, since 2005.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And that Resurrection by Rubens?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It was painted as a memorial for Jan Moretus.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: So the printer and the painter connect.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Good. I like a link.
